items.title: Under fire CEO defends Alice Springs camp 'squalor' after Kumanjayi Little Baby death
items.description: After the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby, the state of Alice Springs's town camps shocked the nation. Now, the man in charge of servicing them is speaking out.

items.title: 'A little perturbed': Trump confirms expletive-laden phone call with Netanyahu
items.description: In an interview with a US podcast, the US president says he was frustrated that Benjamin Netanyahu was "constantly fighting with Lebanon".

items.title: AI slows hiring in some roles, but demand grows for human skills
items.description: A new economic report by consultancy firm Deloitte says the AI "winners" will be organisations that combine human and machine strengths, with recruiters saying human judgement will still be key.

items.title: Australia faces proposed 12.5pc US tariff over forced labour crackdown
items.description: Australia could be hit with a new US tariff after the Trump administration accused dozens of countries of failing to crack down on goods made with forced labour.

items.title: Ukraine strikes St Petersburg oil terminal hours before 'Putin's Davos'
items.description: An oil export terminal was hit hours before the Russian president's annual economic forum got underway.

items.title: Parents of fit 27-year-old asked what quality of life he had by medical staff
items.description: Sam Stubbs's parents were asked about his quality of life while treating him for a lung infection. They realised it was because he was born with Down syndrome.

items.title: Iranian missiles strike Kuwait Airport base injuring dozens of passengers
items.description: At least one person has been killed and more than 60 injured in an attack on Kuwait's international airport, as Iran and the US launch strikes against each other.

items.title: US-Australia talks on AUKUS changes have been underway for 18 months
items.description: The changes announced over the weekend will see Australia buy three second-hand submarines, rather than two second-hand and one new.

items.title: Australia's economy growing at 2.5 per cent annually as slowdown begins
items.description: Australia's economy grew at an annual rate of 2.5 per cent in the March quarter, the same as in the previous quarter.

items.title: Rubio says concerns over Trump's health 'absurd and ridiculous'
items.description: The US president's mental acuity is in the spotlight, with the secretary of state shown videos of Donald Trump appearing to fall asleep during public appearances.

items.title: Neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell broadcasting hate on Instagram from Victorian acreage
items.description: ABC NEWS Verify can reveal that Neo-Nazi leader Thomas Sewell has been uploading antisemitic and homophobic diatribes to Instagram from a property on the outskirts of Melbourne.

items.title: Police investigating people entering New York sewers for unknown reason
items.description: Security cameras have recorded at least three night time instances where groups of people entered or exited sewer tunnels via maintenance holes on streets in Brooklyn and Queens.

items.title: Childcare worker jailed for 'cruel and sadistic' assaults on toddlers
items.description: Queensland childcare worker Edwina Ling has been jailed for four years after pleading guilty to more than 80 counts of assault involving three young children.

items.title: Indonesian official behind food poisoning-plagued meals program arrested
items.description: The ex-chief of Indonesia's free school meals program linked to food poisoning cases has been arrested after a corruption probe.

items.title: Five ways to prevent mould in your home and the best ways to clean it
items.description: Winter is here and with it comes the increased risk of mould in homes, particularly in colder parts of the country. But there are simple ways to keep to it at bay.

items.title: Delhi hotel fire kills at least 21 people, including foreigner visitors
items.description: More than 40 people were injured with some jumping out of the burning building to escape the flames.

items.title: 'Logic becomes clearer': New EV sales record part of trend
items.description: The monthly sales record comes as nearly half of all new vehicles sold last month were either an EV, hybrid, or plug-in hybrid.

items.title: These are the 'worst offenders' in Australian packaging
items.description: A trendy plastic-and-metal takeaway cup used by cafes for iced drinks has been named Australia's worst packaging in the first Unpackit Awards.

items.title: Sydney Morning Herald takes down article after author admits using AI
items.description: The Sydney Morning Herald has taken down an opinion piece defending the use of artificial intelligence at universities, after it emerged its author used AI to write it.

items.title: ABS estimates 80pc of tobacco consumed in Australia last year was illegally sourced
items.description: The experimental estimates are based on "nicotine metabolite concentrations" detected in wastewater samples, combined with data showing a collapse in spending on legal cigarettes and vapes.

items.title: Yacht intercepted by police off Exmouth allegedly carrying outlaw gang member
items.description: WA Police and Australian Federal Police intercepted a yacht off the coast of Exmouth in northern WA which allegedly had a Queensland fugitive on board.

items.title: Why Hugh Jackman's brother cried on his first day as a prison-school teacher
items.description: After Ralph Jackman retrained as a teacher, his first job was in a youth detention centre. His new memoir reveals how a broken system is failing vulnerable kids.

items.title: Singer known for Disney's Aladdin hit duet A Whole New World dies
items.description: Peabo Bryson, known for his Grammy and Oscar-winning Disney collaborations, has died at 75.

items.title: Hollywood legend set to bring Finke Desert Race to the big screen
items.description: The gruelling outback Finke Desert Race is set for Hollywood treatment after Marvel's Chris Hemsworth backs a feature-length movie.

items.title: Defence plans to sell Sydney Harbour land Albanese once fought to protect
items.description: Parliamentary speeches from 2021 reveal the prime minister was opposed to privatising Sydney Harbour land now being sold off by the Defence Department.
